Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 68, verse 1–3:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe, (1) You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman. (2) Indeed, for you is a reward never cut off. (3)﴾

The exegetes differed concerning the interpretation of His saying: ﴿Nun﴾. Some of them said: It is the fish upon which the earths rest.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdiyy related to us, from Shuʿbah, from Sulayman, from Abu Zabyan, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The first thing God created was the pen, and it ran with what would occur. Then He raised up vapour of water, and the heavens were created from it. Then He created the Nun, and the earth was spread out upon the back of the Nun. The earth shook and swayed, so it was steadied with the mountains, for the mountains boast over the earth. He said: And he recited: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe﴾.

Tamim ibn al-Muntasir related to us, saying: Ishaq related to us, from Sharik, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu Zabyan, or Mujahid, from Ibn ʿAbbas, with its like, except that he said: "the heavens were split open from it."

Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Yahya related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, saying: Sulayman related to me, from Abu Zabyan, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The first thing God created was the pen. He said: Write. It said: What shall I write? He said: Write the decree. So it ran with what would happen from that day until the Hour arises. Then He created the Nun and raised up vapour of water, and the heaven was split open from it, and the earth was spread out upon the back of the Nun. The Nun quivered, so the earth swayed, and it was steadied with the mountains, for they boast over the earth.

Wasil ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Fudayl related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu Zabyan, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "The first thing God created was the pen. He said to it: Write. It said: What shall I write? He said: Write the decree. So the pen ran with what would be until the Hour arises. Then He raised up vapour of water and split the heavens from it. Then He created the Nun, and the earth was spread out upon its back. The Nun quivered, so the earth swayed, and it was steadied with the mountains, for they boast over the earth."

Wasil ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Waki related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu Zabyan, from Ibn ʿAbbas, similarly.

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to us, saying: Abu ʿAsim related to us, saying: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqaʾ related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, that Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr informed him, from Mujahid, who said: It used to be said that the Nun is the fish beneath the seventh earth.

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, saying: Maʿmar said, al-Aʿmash related to us, that Ibn ʿAbbas said: The first thing created was the pen, then he mentioned something like the report of Wasil from Ibn Fudayl, and added in it: Then Ibn ʿAbbas recited: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe﴾.

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from ʿAta, from Abu al-Duha Muslim ibn Subayh, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The first thing my Lord created was the pen. He said to it: Write. So it wrote what would occur until the Hour arises. Then He created the Nun above the water, then He pressed the earth down upon it.

Others said: ﴿Nun﴾ is a letter of the name al-Rahman.

Mention of those who said that:

ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Marwazi related to us, saying: ʿAli ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Yazid, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿Alif-Lam-Ra﴾, ﴿Ha-Mim﴾ and ﴿Nun﴾ are separated letters of al-Rahman.

Muhammad ibn Maʿmar related to me, saying: ʿAbbas ibn Ziyad al-Bahili related to us, saying: Shuʿbah related to us, from Abu Bishr, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Alif-Lam-Ra﴾, ﴿Ha-Mim﴾ and ﴿Nun﴾, he said: It is a separated name.

Others said: ﴿Nun﴾ is the inkwell, and "the pen" is the pen.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Yaʿqub related to us, saying: My brother ʿIsa ibn ʿAbd Allah related to us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: God created the Nun, which is the inkwell, and created the pen, and said: Write. It said: What shall I write? He said: Write what will occur until the Day of Resurrection: deeds done, righteous or wicked, and provision apportioned, lawful or unlawful. Then He fixed for each of these its matter: its entry into the world, its duration in it, and how it leaves it. Then He placed over the servants guardians and for the Book keepers. The guardians copy each day the deeds of that day. When provision is exhausted and traces cease and the term is ended, the guardians come seeking the deeds of that day, and the keepers say to them: We find nothing for your companion with us. So the guardians return and find that they have died. He said: Ibn ʿAbbas said: Are you not an Arab people who hear the guardians saying: ﴿Indeed We used to transcribe what you were doing﴾? Is copying anything but from an original?

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Hasan and Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Nun﴾, he said: It is the inkwell.

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Bashir related to us, saying: ʿAmr related to us, from Qatadah, who said: The Nun is the inkwell.

Others said: ﴿Nun﴾ is a tablet of light.

Mention of those who said that:

al-Hasan ibn Shabib al-Muktib related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Jazari related to us, from Furat ibn Abi al-Furat, from Muʿawiyah ibn Qurrah, from his father, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe﴾: a tablet of light, running with what will occur until the Day of Resurrection."

Others said: ﴿Nun﴾ is an oath which God swore by.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe﴾: God swears by whatever He wills.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe﴾: This is an oath which God swore by.

Others said: it is the name of a surah.

Others said: it is one of the letters of the alphabet. We have already mentioned the discussion of similar letters of the alphabet with which the opening of surahs begin, and the discussion of this verse is like that discussion.

The reciters differed in reading ﴿Nun﴾. The majority of the reciters of Kufa, except al-Kisa'i, and the majority of the reciters of Basra, made the nun clear there and in ﴿Ya-Sin﴾, because it is a letter of spelling, and spelling is based on pausing upon it even when connected. Al-Kisa'i would assimilate the final nun of them and suppress it, based on connection.

The correct view in this matter, in our opinion, is that both are eloquent readings, and whichever the reader recites is correct; however, making the nun clear is more eloquent and more well-known, so it is more pleasing to me. As for "al-qalam" (the pen), it is the well-known pen, except that the pen by which our Lord swore is the pen which God, may His remembrance be exalted, created, and commanded, so it ran by writing all that would be until the Day of Resurrection.

Muhammad ibn Salih al-Anmati related to me, saying: ʿAbbad ibn al-ʿAwwam related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Sulaym related to us, saying: I heard ʿAta say: I asked al-Walid ibn ʿUbadah ibn al-Samit: How was your father's will when death gathered him? He said: He called me and said: O my son, fear God, and know that you will not fear God until you believe in God alone, and in the decree, its good and its evil. I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "The first thing God created was the pen. He said to it: Write. It said: O Lord, what shall I write? He said: Write the decree. So the pen ran at that hour with what was and what will be forever."

Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Tusi related to me, saying: ʿAli ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq related to us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mubarak informed us, saying: Rabah ibn Zayd informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Habib, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, that he used to narrate that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The first thing God created was the pen, and He commanded it, so it wrote everything."

Musa ibn Sahl al-Ramli related to us, saying: Nuʿaym ibn Hammad related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak related to us with his chain from the Prophet (ﷺ), similarly.

Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Abu Hashim, from Mujahid, who said: I said to Ibn ʿAbbas: Some people deny the decree. He said: They deny the Book of God. I will surely seize the hair of one of them, and he will not be able to hold it. God was upon His Throne before He created anything, and the first thing God created was the pen, so it ran with what would occur until the Day of Resurrection. People only act upon a matter that has already been finished.

Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Samad related to us, saying: Shuʿbah related to us, saying: Abu Hashim related to us, that he heard Mujahid say: I heard ʿAbd Allah, we do not know whether he meant Ibn ʿUmar or Ibn ʿAbbas, say: The first thing God created was the pen, and the pen ran with what would be; and people only act today in what has already been finished.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Muʿawiyah ibn Salih related to me; and ʿAbd Allah ibn Adam related to me, saying: my father related to us, saying: al-Layth ibn Saʿd related to us, from Muʿawiyah ibn Salih, from Ayyub ibn Ziyad, who said: ʿAbbad ibn al-Walid ibn ʿUbadah ibn al-Samit related to me, saying: my father informed me, who said: ʿUbadah ibn al-Samit said: O my son, I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "The first thing God created was the pen, and He said to it: Write. So it ran at that hour with what will be until the Day of Resurrection."

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim related to us, saying: ʿIsa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Nun. By the pen﴾, he said: It is that with which the Remembrance was written.

al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqaʾ related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, who informed him, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Nun. By the pen﴾, he said: It is that with which the Remembrance was written.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and what they inscribe﴾:

It means: and those who write and inscribe. When the interpretation is directed to this meaning, the oath is by the creatures and their actions. The speech may also bear another meaning, which is that "what" means the act of inscribing, so the oath is by the writing, as if it were said: Nun, by the pen and the writing.

The exegetes related the like of what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and what they inscribe﴾: "they scratch."

ʿAli related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Muʿawiyah related to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿and what they inscribe﴾: it means: they write.

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim related to us, saying: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqaʾ related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿and what they inscribe﴾: "and what they write."

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and what they inscribe﴾: "and what they write." It is said of it: sataра fulan al-kitab, fa-huwa yasturu satran, meaning he wrote it. From it is the saying of Ru'bah ibn al-Ajjaj:

"Indeed I, and lines that were inscribed in lines"¹

* *

As for His saying: ﴿You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman﴾:

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman, refuting by this the polytheists of Quraysh who said to him: You are mad.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, for you is a reward never cut off﴾:

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed for you, O Muhammad, is a great reward from God for your patience over the harm the polytheists inflicted upon you, undiminished and uninterrupted, from their saying: a rope is "matin" (firm) when it is strong, and its strength has weakened when its power has weakened.

Mujahid used to say about this:

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related this to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim related to us, saying: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqaʾ related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿never cut off﴾: he said: "counted."

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim related to us, saying: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqaʾ related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿and what they inscribe﴾: "and what they write."

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and what they inscribe﴾: "and what they write." It is said of it: sataра fulan al-kitab, fa-huwa yasturu satran, meaning he wrote it. From it is the saying of Ru'bah ibn al-Ajjaj:

"Indeed I, and lines that were inscribed in lines"¹

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, for you is a reward never cut off﴾:

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed for you, O Muhammad, is a great reward from God for your patience over the harm the polytheists inflicted upon you, undiminished and uninterrupted, from their saying: a rope is "matin" (firm) when it is strong, and its strength has weakened when its power has weakened.

Mujahid used to say about this:

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related this to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim related to us, saying: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqaʾ related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿never cut off﴾: he said: "counted."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 68, verse 1–3:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe, (1) You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman. (2) Indeed, for you is a reward never cut off. (3)﴾

The exegetes differed concerning the interpretation of His saying: ﴿Nun﴾. Some of them said: It is the fish upon which the earths rest.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdiyy related to us, from Shuʿbah, from Sulayman, from Abu Zabyan, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The first thing God created was the pen, and it ran with what would occur. Then He raised up vapour of water, and the heavens were created from it. Then He created the Nun, and the earth was spread out upon the back of the Nun. The earth shook and swayed, so it was steadied with the mountains, for the mountains boast over the earth. He said: And he recited: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe﴾.

Tamim ibn al-Muntasir related to us, saying: Ishaq related to us, from Sharik, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu Zabyan, or Mujahid, from Ibn ʿAbbas, with its like, except that he said: "the heavens were split open from it."

Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Yahya related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, saying: Sulayman related to me, from Abu Zabyan, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The first thing God created was the pen. He said: Write. It said: What shall I write? He said: Write the decree. So it ran with what would happen from that day until the Hour arises. Then He created the Nun and raised up vapour of water, and the heaven was split open from it, and the earth was spread out upon the back of the Nun. The Nun quivered, so the earth swayed, and it was steadied with the mountains, for they boast over the earth.

Wasil ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Fudayl related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu Zabyan, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "The first thing God created was the pen. He said to it: Write. It said: What shall I write? He said: Write the decree. So the pen ran with what would be until the Hour arises. Then He raised up vapour of water and split the heavens from it. Then He created the Nun, and the earth was spread out upon its back. The Nun quivered, so the earth swayed, and it was steadied with the mountains, for they boast over the earth."

Wasil ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Waki related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu Zabyan, from Ibn ʿAbbas, similarly.

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to us, saying: Abu ʿAsim related to us, saying: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqaʾ related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, that Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr informed him, from Mujahid, who said: It used to be said that the Nun is the fish beneath the seventh earth.

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, saying: Maʿmar said, al-Aʿmash related to us, that Ibn ʿAbbas said: The first thing created was the pen, then he mentioned something like the report of Wasil from Ibn Fudayl, and added in it: Then Ibn ʿAbbas recited: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe﴾.

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from ʿAta, from Abu al-Duha Muslim ibn Subayh, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The first thing my Lord created was the pen. He said to it: Write. So it wrote what would occur until the Hour arises. Then He created the Nun above the water, then He pressed the earth down upon it.

Others said: ﴿Nun﴾ is a letter of the name al-Rahman.

Mention of those who said that:

ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Marwazi related to us, saying: ʿAli ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Yazid, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿Alif-Lam-Ra﴾, ﴿Ha-Mim﴾ and ﴿Nun﴾ are separated letters of al-Rahman.

Muhammad ibn Maʿmar related to me, saying: ʿAbbas ibn Ziyad al-Bahili related to us, saying: Shuʿbah related to us, from Abu Bishr, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Alif-Lam-Ra﴾, ﴿Ha-Mim﴾ and ﴿Nun﴾, he said: It is a separated name.

Others said: ﴿Nun﴾ is the inkwell, and "the pen" is the pen.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Yaʿqub related to us, saying: My brother ʿIsa ibn ʿAbd Allah related to us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: God created the Nun, which is the inkwell, and created the pen, and said: Write. It said: What shall I write? He said: Write what will occur until the Day of Resurrection: deeds done, righteous or wicked, and provision apportioned, lawful or unlawful. Then He fixed for each of these its matter: its entry into the world, its duration in it, and how it leaves it. Then He placed over the servants guardians and for the Book keepers. The guardians copy each day the deeds of that day. When provision is exhausted and traces cease and the term is ended, the guardians come seeking the deeds of that day, and the keepers say to them: We find nothing for your companion with us. So the guardians return and find that they have died. He said: Ibn ʿAbbas said: Are you not an Arab people who hear the guardians saying: ﴿Indeed We used to transcribe what you were doing﴾? Is copying anything but from an original?

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Hasan and Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Nun﴾, he said: It is the inkwell.

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Bashir related to us, saying: ʿAmr related to us, from Qatadah, who said: The Nun is the inkwell.

Others said: ﴿Nun﴾ is a tablet of light.

Mention of those who said that:

al-Hasan ibn Shabib al-Muktib related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Jazari related to us, from Furat ibn Abi al-Furat, from Muʿawiyah ibn Qurrah, from his father, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe﴾: a tablet of light, running with what will occur until the Day of Resurrection."

Others said: ﴿Nun﴾ is an oath which God swore by.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe﴾: God swears by whatever He wills.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe﴾: This is an oath which God swore by.

Others said: it is the name of a surah.

Others said: it is one of the letters of the alphabet. We have already mentioned the discussion of similar letters of the alphabet with which the opening of surahs begin, and the discussion of this verse is like that discussion.

The reciters differed in reading ﴿Nun﴾. The majority of the reciters of Kufa, except al-Kisa'i, and the majority of the reciters of Basra, made the nun clear there and in ﴿Ya-Sin﴾, because it is a letter of spelling, and spelling is based on pausing upon it even when connected. Al-Kisa'i would assimilate the final nun of them and suppress it, based on connection.

The correct view in this matter, in our opinion, is that both are eloquent readings, and whichever the reader recites is correct; however, making the nun clear is more eloquent and more well-known, so it is more pleasing to me. As for "al-qalam" (the pen), it is the well-known pen, except that the pen by which our Lord swore is the pen which God, may His remembrance be exalted, created, and commanded, so it ran by writing all that would be until the Day of Resurrection.

Muhammad ibn Salih al-Anmati related to me, saying: ʿAbbad ibn al-ʿAwwam related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Sulaym related to us, saying: I heard ʿAta say: I asked al-Walid ibn ʿUbadah ibn al-Samit: How was your father's will when death gathered him? He said: He called me and said: O my son, fear God, and know that you will not fear God until you believe in God alone, and in the decree, its good and its evil. I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "The first thing God created was the pen. He said to it: Write. It said: O Lord, what shall I write? He said: Write the decree. So the pen ran at that hour with what was and what will be forever."

Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Tusi related to me, saying: ʿAli ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq related to us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mubarak informed us, saying: Rabah ibn Zayd informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Habib, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, that he used to narrate that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The first thing God created was the pen, and He commanded it, so it wrote everything."

Musa ibn Sahl al-Ramli related to us, saying: Nuʿaym ibn Hammad related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak related to us with his chain from the Prophet (ﷺ), similarly.

Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Abu Hashim, from Mujahid, who said: I said to Ibn ʿAbbas: Some people deny the decree. He said: They deny the Book of God. I will surely seize the hair of one of them, and he will not be able to hold it. God was upon His Throne before He created anything, and the first thing God created was the pen, so it ran with what would occur until the Day of Resurrection. People only act upon a matter that has already been finished.

Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Samad related to us, saying: Shuʿbah related to us, saying: Abu Hashim related to us, that he heard Mujahid say: I heard ʿAbd Allah, we do not know whether he meant Ibn ʿUmar or Ibn ʿAbbas, say: The first thing God created was the pen, and the pen ran with what would be; and people only act today in what has already been finished.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Muʿawiyah ibn Salih related to me; and ʿAbd Allah ibn Adam related to me, saying: my father related to us, saying: al-Layth ibn Saʿd related to us, from Muʿawiyah ibn Salih, from Ayyub ibn Ziyad, who said: ʿAbbad ibn al-Walid ibn ʿUbadah ibn al-Samit related to me, saying: my father informed me, who said: ʿUbadah ibn al-Samit said: O my son, I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "The first thing God created was the pen, and He said to it: Write. So it ran at that hour with what will be until the Day of Resurrection."

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim related to us, saying: ʿIsa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Nun. By the pen﴾, he said: It is that with which the Remembrance was written.

al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqaʾ related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, who informed him, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Nun. By the pen﴾, he said: It is that with which the Remembrance was written.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and what they inscribe﴾:

It means: and those who write and inscribe. When the interpretation is directed to this meaning, the oath is by the creatures and their actions. The speech may also bear another meaning, which is that "what" means the act of inscribing, so the oath is by the writing, as if it were said: Nun, by the pen and the writing.

The exegetes related the like of what we have said.

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed for you, O Muhammad, is a great reward from God for your patience over the harm the polytheists inflicted upon you, undiminished and uninterrupted, from their saying: a rope is "matin" (firm) when it is strong, and its strength has weakened when its power has weakened.

Mujahid used to say about this:

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related this to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim related to us, saying: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqaʾ related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿never cut off﴾: he said: "counted."

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 68, verses 4–7:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And indeed, you are of a great character (khuluq 'azim)﴾ [68:4] ﴿So you will see and they will see﴾ [68:5] ﴿which of you is the afflicted (al-maftun)﴾ [68:6] ﴿Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of those who are guided﴾ [68:7]

Mention of those who said that:

* Ali related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And indeed, you are of a great character﴾, he said: "a great religion."

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And indeed, you are of a great character﴾, he said: "You are upon a great religion, which is Islam."

* Ubayd ibn Asbat related to us, he said: my father related to me, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq, from Atiyya, regarding His words: ﴿And indeed, you are of a great character﴾, he said: "The adab of the Qur'an."

And His words: ﴿So you will see and they will see﴾

God, may He be remembered, says: "So you, O Muhammad, will see, and the polytheists of your people who call you mad will see, ﴿which of you is the afflicted﴾."

The people of interpretation said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

* al-Husayn related to us, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd related to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿So you will see and they will see﴾, he said: "you will see and they will see."

* * *

And His words: ﴿which of you is the afflicted﴾

The people of interpretation differed about its interpretation. Some of them said: its interpretation is "which of you is the madman," as if they directed the meaning of the ba' in His words ﴿bi-ayyikum﴾ to the meaning of "in" (fi). When the ba' is directed to the meaning of "in," the sense of the statement becomes: "and they will see in which of the two groups the madman is, in your group, O Muhammad, or their group," and al-maftun becomes a noun raised by the ba'.

Mention of those who said the meaning is: "which of you is the madman."

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Mujahid: ﴿bi-ayyikum al-maftun﴾, he said: "the madman."

* He said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Khusayf, from Mujahid: ﴿bi-ayyikum al-maftun﴾, he said: "which of you is the madman."

Others said: rather, its interpretation is: "which of you is the madness (al-junun)." It seems that those who said this understood al-maftun to mean the act of afflicting (al-fitna) or the afflicted, as it is said: "he has neither intellect (ma'qul) nor binding (ma'qud)," meaning he has no intellect nor firm opinion; so likewise al-maftun is placed in the position of al-futun.

Mention of those who said: al-maftun has the sense of the verbal noun and the sense of madness:

* Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, he said: Abu Asim related to us, he said: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿bi-ayyikum al-maftun﴾, he said: "the Devil."

* I was told by al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd related to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿bi-ayyikum al-maftun﴾, he means "the madness."

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas who said: "which of you is the madness."

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: "which of you is more deserving of the Devil." On the view of these, the ba' is an added particle whose presence and absence are equivalent, and these people illustrated this with the verse of the rajaz poet:

nahnu banu Ja'da ashab al-falaj
nadribu bi-l-sayfi wa narjū bi-l-faraj

[These two verses are from the rajaz meter, and they are among the examples cited by Abu Ubayda in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 179) ... The evidence in it is that the ba' in his words "bi-l-faraj" means "narju al-faraj," just as it is added in the verse. The two verses are by al-Nabigha al-Ja'di. This was cited earlier for a similar passage in volume 18, p. 14, so refer to it.]

meaning: "we hope for relief," so the presence of the ba' in this place is, in their view, equivalent to its absence.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿So you will see and they will see, which of you is the afflicted﴾, he said: "which of you is more deserving of the Devil."

* Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿which of you is the afflicted﴾, he said: "which of you is more deserving of the Devil."

The grammarians (ahl al-'arabiyya) differed on this in the same way the exegetes differed. Some grammarians of Basra said: the meaning is: "So you will see and they will see which of you is the afflicted." Some grammarians of Kufa said: "bi-ayyikum al-maftun" here means "madness," and it is in the manner of al-futun, as they say: "he has neither intellect nor binding." He said: If you wish, you may make "bi-ayyikum" in "ayyikum" in "which of the two groups is the madman," and then it is a noun, not a verbal noun.

The most correct of these views in my opinion is the view of the one who said: the meaning is "which of you is the madness," and he directed al-maftun to al-futun in the sense of a verbal noun, because this is the most apparent meaning of the statement, when one does not intend the ba' to be dropped, and we make its presence have an understandable purpose.

We have already shown that it is impossible for the Qur'an to contain anything without meaning.

* * *

And His words: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way﴾

God, may He be remembered, says: "Indeed, your Lord, O Muhammad, is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, like the straying of the disbelievers of Quraysh from the religion of God and the path of guidance. ﴿And He is most knowing of those who are guided﴾" means: "And He is most knowing of who was guided, who followed the truth and acknowledged it, just as you were guided and followed the truth." This is from the indirect forms of speech (ma'arid al-kalam). The meaning of the statement is: "Indeed your Lord, O Muhammad, knows you best, and you are the guided one, and your people, the disbelievers of Quraysh, are the ones who have strayed from the path of truth."

God, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "And indeed, you, O Muhammad, are of a great character (adab 'azim)." That is the adab of the Qur'an, with which God educated him, and it is Islam and its laws.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Mujahid: ﴿bi-ayyikum al-maftun﴾, he said: "the madman."

Mention of those who said: al-maftun has the sense of the verbal noun and the sense of madness:

He said: If you wish, you may make "bi-ayyikum" in "ayyikum" in "which of the two groups is the madman," and then it is a noun, not a verbal noun.

The most correct of these views in my opinion is the view of the one who said: the meaning is "which of you is the madness," and he directed al-maftun to al-futun in the sense of a verbal noun, because this is the most apparent meaning of the statement, when one does not intend the ba' to be dropped, and we make its presence have an understandable purpose.

We have already shown that it is impossible for the Qur'an to contain anything without meaning.

* * *

And His words: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way﴾

God, may He be remembered, says: "Indeed, your Lord, O Muhammad, is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, like the straying of the disbelievers of Quraysh from the religion of God and the path of guidance. ﴿And He is most knowing of those who are guided﴾" means: "And He is most knowing of who was guided, who followed the truth and acknowledged it, just as you were guided and followed the truth." This is from the indirect forms of speech (ma'arid al-kalam). The meaning of the statement is: "Indeed your Lord, O Muhammad, knows you best, and you are the guided one, and your people, the disbelievers of Quraysh, are the ones who have strayed from the path of truth."

And do not obey, O Muhammad, every one who swears excessively by falsehood. ﴿Contemptible﴾: he is the weak.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

However, some of them directed the meaning of "contemptible" to mean the liar, and I think he did that because he saw that when someone is described as contemptible, he is described so due to the contempt of his own self upon him, and likewise the description of one who lies frequently: he lies due to the contempt of his own self upon him.

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿every habitual swearer, contemptible﴾, and "contemptible": the liar.

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿habitual swearer, contemptible﴾, he said: weak.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And do not obey every habitual swearer, contemptible﴾, and he is the one who is excessive in evil.

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: ﴿every habitual swearer, contemptible﴾, he said: every one who swears excessively is contemptible and weak.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Sa'id, from al-Hasan and Qatadah: ﴿And do not obey every habitual swearer, contemptible﴾, he said: he is the one who is excessive in evil.

* *

His saying: ﴿A slanderer﴾

That is: one who backbites people, eating their flesh.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿a slanderer﴾, he said: meaning backbiting.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿a slanderer﴾, eating the flesh of the Muslims.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿a slanderer﴾: "The hammaz is the one who pushes people with his hand and strikes them, not with the tongue." And he recited: ﴿Woe to every scorner and mocker﴾, the one who mocks people with his tongue. And the root of hamz is ghamz (pressing), so the backbiter is called hammaz, because he attacks people's honor with what they dislike, and that is a pressing upon them.

* *

His saying: ﴿going about with malicious gossip﴾

He says: going about carrying people's talk about one another, transmitting the words of some of them to others.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿going about with malicious gossip﴾: walking about with falsehood.

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Kalbi, regarding His saying: ﴿going about with malicious gossip﴾, he said: he is al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, originally from Thaqif, and his affiliation was among the Banu Zuhrah.

As for His saying, ﴿zanim﴾:

The zanim in the speech of the Arabs is one attached to a people while not being of them. From it is the verse of Hassan ibn Thabit:

"You are a zanim, attached among the family of Hashim, as the single cup is attached behind the rider."

[The line is among the evidences cited by Abu ʿUbayda in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 179 of the University photocopy 26390, from the manuscript "Murad Mullah" in Istanbul), which he recited at the words of God Most High: (zanim). He said: The zanim: the one hung among a people while not being of them. Hassan ibn Thabit said: "And you are zanim..." the verse. It is said of the male goat: zanim, having two zanmas (wattles).]

Another said:

"A zanim, who does not know who his father is, the son of a whore, of base lineage."

[This verse is not among the evidences of al-Farra' nor of Abu ʿUbayda, and the author did not attribute it to its speaker. In Lisan: the zanim: one who is attached among a people while not being of them, needed by no one, as if he is among them a zanma (the wattle of a goat hanging at its throat). He says: he is among them a zanim, they do not know his father, because he is an intruder. His mother is a prostitute, and his lineage is base. It has the same meaning as the previous verse on the sense of "zanim."]

And the interpreters of the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

He says: he is among them a zanim, they do not know his father, because he is an intruder. His mother is a prostitute, and his lineage is base. It has the same meaning as the previous verse on the sense of "zanim."]

And the interpreters of the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

On the interpretation of His words, "Who is possessed of wealth and children, when Our verses are recited to him he says, 'Legends of the ancients.' We shall brand him upon the snout." (68:14–16)

The reciters differed over the reading of His words, "an kāna" (that he is). Abū Ja'far al-Madanī and Ḥamzah recited it as "a-an kāna dhā māl" with two hamzahs, in the interrogative form. The reading of those who recited it this way may be understood in two ways:

The first is that it is intended as a rebuke of this despicable oath-taker, so that the meaning is: "Because he is possessed of wealth and children, when Our verses are recited to him he says, 'Legends of the ancients'?" This is the more evident of the two interpretations.

The second is that it is intended as: "Because he is possessed of wealth and children, will you obey him?" in the manner of reproach toward those who obeyed him. The rest of the reciters of Madinah, Kufah and Basrah recited it as "an kāna dhā māl," in the declarative form without the interrogative hamzah. Its meaning, when recited thus, is: "Do not obey every despicable oath-taker, [merely] because he is possessed of wealth and children." It is as though He forbade him to obey such a person on account of his wealth and children.

* *

As for His words, "When Our verses are recited to him, he says, 'Legends of the ancients,'"

the meaning is: when Our Book's verses are recited to him, he says, "This is what the ancients wrote," mocking it and denying that it is from God.

* *

As for His words, "We shall brand him upon the snout,"

the commentators differed in its interpretation. Some of them said: its meaning is, "We shall mark him with the sword, making that a lasting sign and a permanent mark upon him as long as he lives."

Those who said this:

Muḥammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbās, regarding "We shall brand him upon the snout": he fought on the day of Badr, and was struck on the snout by the sword in the fighting.

Others said: rather, its meaning is "We shall brand him with a lasting disgrace."

Those who said this:

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words, "We shall brand him upon the snout": a disgrace that will not leave him, the last of what is upon him.

Others said: "We shall brand him" means "upon his nose."

Those who said this:

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding "We shall brand him upon the snout," he said: "We shall brand him upon his nose."

The most correct of the two views regarding its interpretation, in my opinion, is the view of the one who said: its meaning is, "We shall make his condition clear with an evident clarity, so that people recognize him and it is not hidden from them, just as a brand is not hidden on the snout."

Qatadah said: its meaning is a disgrace that will not leave him, the last of what is upon him. It may also possibly be that he was struck with the sword, so that for him there is combined, together with the clarification of his defects to people, the striking with the sword.

By His words, "We shall brand him" (sanasimuhu) is meant: "We shall cauterize him." Some of them said: its meaning is, "We shall brand him with the brand of the people of the Fire," that is, "We shall blacken his face."

He said: although the snout has been singled out for the brand, it is in the sense of the face, because part of the face stands for part of it, and the Arabs say, "By God, I will brand you with a brand that will not leave you," meaning the nose. He said: one of them recited to me:

*"la-u'allinnahu wasman lā yufāriquhu / kamā yuḥazzu biḥammā al-mīsami al-najar"*

[The line is among the citations of al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 339), where he said regarding the verse "We shall brand him upon the snout": that is, "We shall brand him with the brand of the people of the Fire," that is, "We shall blacken his face." Although the snout has been singled out for the brand, it is in the sense of the face, because part of the face stands for part of it. The Arabs say, "By God, I will brand you with a brand that will not leave you," meaning the nose. One of them recited to me: "la-u'allinnahu wasman," the line... He said: al-mīsam is the iron with which one brands, and al-bahr is the camel that has been struck by the disease that causes it to be branded for it. Ibn al-A'rabi's... [remainder of Farra's citation continues as in the source] — Ed. note in the source: the lexicographer Ibn Manzur cites the line under "bahr"; al-Farra' said bahr is that a camel drinks water excessively until it is struck by a disease, and when the disease strikes it is cauterized in places and it recovers. Al-Azhari, commenting on him, said: the disease that strikes a camel so that it is not quenched by water is al-najar, with nūn and jīm, and al-bajar with bā' and jīm. As for al-bahr, it is a disease that causes consumption; one whose consumption has seized him is "abhara"; a man who is baḥīr or baḥr is one wasted and gone in flesh, on the authority of Ibn al-A'rabi. I say: this is supported by what came in Lisan al-'Arab under "najar": al-Jawhari said: al-najar, with a vowel on the first letter, is thirst that strikes camels and sheep from eating the fruit of the bitter-tree (ḥabba), so that they can hardly be quenched with water; it is said, "najarat al-ibil" and "mujarat" also. In al-Tahdhib: najara yanjuru najaran, if one drinks much water and cannot be quenched; Ya'qub said: it may strike a human as well.]

And al-ḥamā al-mīsam is its heat, and al-mīsam is an iron with which one brands.

And al-najar is a disease that afflicts camels, so that they are branded on their noses.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 68, verses 17–18**

**On the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, exalted is He:** ﴿Indeed, We have tested them as We tested the people of the garden, when they swore that they would surely harvest its fruit in the morning, and did not make an exception (inshallah)﴾ (17–18).

He, exalted is His remembrance, means by His words ﴿Indeed, We have tested them﴾: that is, We have tested the polytheists of Quraysh. He says: We tried them and examined them. ﴿as We tested the people of the garden﴾: as We tried the owners of the orchard. ﴿when they swore that they would surely harvest its fruit in the morning﴾: when they swore that they would surely cut its fruit when they arose in the morning. ﴿and did not make an exception﴾: and did not say "if God wills."

Ahl al-ta'wil (the scholars of interpretation) have said according to what we have said on this.

**Those who said this:**

Hannad ibn al-Sari narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Simak, from Ikrimah, regarding His words ﴿No poor man shall enter it today against you﴾: "They were people from Abyssinia. Their father had a garden from which he fed the poor. When their father died, his sons said: 'By God, our father was foolish when he fed the poor. So let us swear that we will surely harvest it in the morning, and let us not make an exception, and let us not feed a poor man.'"

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿they would surely harvest it in the morning﴾: "The garden belonged to an old man who used to give charity. His sons would forbid him from giving charity. He would keep the provision of his year and spend and give away the surplus in charity. When their father died, they went out to it and said: ﴿No poor man shall enter it today against you﴾."

**It is also mentioned that the people of the garden were People of the Book.**

**Those who said this:**

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, We have tested them as We tested the people of the garden, when they swore...﴾ ... the verse. He said: "They were from among the People of the Book. Al-sarm means cutting off, and by His words ﴿they would surely harvest it﴾ He meant they would surely pick its fruit. From this is the verse of Imru' al-Qays:

*Da'd has cut you off after you were in continuous union,*
*and there appeared to Da'd some of what appears.* [[The author attributed the verse to Imru' al-Qays, but I have not found it in Mukhtar al-Shi'r al-Jahili, nor in al-Iqd al-Samin, and perhaps it is by someone other than Imru' al-Qays ibn Hujr al-Kindi, from al-Muraqqish. The author recited it as evidence that al-sarm in His words (liyasrimunnaha) means cutting off. In (Lisan al-Arab: sarm) al-sarm is decisive cutting off. Some of them generalised it to cutting off of any kind. End.]]

**On the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, exalted is He:** ﴿Indeed, We have tested them as We tested the people of the garden, when they swore that they would surely harvest its fruit in the morning, and did not make an exception (inshallah)﴾ (17–18).

He, exalted is His remembrance, means by His words ﴿Indeed, We have tested them﴾: that is, We have tested the polytheists of Quraysh. He says: We tried them and examined them. ﴿as We tested the people of the garden﴾: as We tried the owners of the orchard. ﴿when they swore that they would surely harvest its fruit in the morning﴾: when they swore that they would surely cut its fruit when they arose in the morning. ﴿and did not make an exception﴾: and did not say "if God wills."

Ahl al-ta'wil (the scholars of interpretation) have said according to what we have said on this.

**Those who said this:**

Hannad ibn al-Sari narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Simak, from Ikrimah, regarding His words ﴿No poor man shall enter it today against you﴾: "They were people from Abyssinia. Their father had a garden from which he fed the poor. When their father died, his sons said: 'By God, our father was foolish when he fed the poor. So let us swear that we will surely harvest it in the morning, and let us not make an exception, and let us not feed a poor man.'"

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿they would surely harvest it in the morning﴾: "The garden belonged to an old man who used to give charity. His sons would forbid him from giving charity. He would keep the provision of his year and spend and give away the surplus in charity. When their father died, they went out to it and said: ﴿No poor man shall enter it today against you﴾."

**It is also mentioned that the people of the garden were People of the Book.**

**Those who said this:**

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, We have tested them as We tested the people of the garden, when they swore...﴾ ... the verse. He said: "They were from among the People of the Book. Al-sarm means cutting off, and by His words ﴿they would surely harvest it﴾ He meant they would surely pick its fruit. From this is the verse of Imru' al-Qays:

*Da'd has cut you off after you were in continuous union,*
*and there appeared to Da'd some of what appears.* [[The author attributed the verse to Imru' al-Qays, but I have not found it in Mukhtar al-Shi'r al-Jahili, nor in al-Iqd al-Samin, and perhaps it is by someone other than Imru' al-Qays ibn Hujr al-Kindi, from al-Muraqqish. The author recited it as evidence that al-sarm in His words (liyasrimunnaha) means cutting off. In (Lisan al-Arab: sarm) al-sarm is decisive cutting off. Some of them generalised it to cutting off of any kind. End.]]

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then there passed over it a visitation from your Lord while they were asleep﴾ [68:19] ﴿so it became like the black night (al-sarim)﴾ [68:20].

He, Exalted is He, says: A visitor from the command of God came by night to the garden of these people while they were asleep. In the speech of the Arabs, "al-ta'if" (the visitor) is used only at night, never by day, though they may say: "I circled around it (atfu bihā) by day."

Al-Farra' mentions that Abu al-Jarrah recited to him:

"I circled around it by day, not by night, and the desire for young ewes (al-rikhal) distracted its lord."

[[The verse is cited by al-Farra' in his Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 393) at His saying (Then there passed over it a visitation from your Lord while they were asleep). He said: "The visitor (al-ta'if) is only at night, never by day, though the Arabs have spoken it, saying: 'I circled around it by day,' and it is not placed in the daytime, but it is in the same position as your saying: 'If the sandgrouse (al-qata) were left at night, it would sleep,' because the sandgrouse does not travel at night." He said: "Abu al-Jarrah al-Uqayli recited to me: 'I circled around it by day..' the verse." End of quote. Al-rikhal: the plural of rakhl (with kasra or fatha on the ra'): the female of the young of sheep; the male is hamal; the plural is arkhul and rikhal (with kasra or damma) and also rikhlan. End of quote.]]

Al-rikhal are the female young of sheep.

The people of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said regarding the meaning of this.

Those who said so:

Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Salt told us, saying: Abu Kurayb told us, from Qabus, from his father, who said: I asked Ibn Abbas about al-tawafan (the circling), "Then there passed over it a visitation from your Lord," and he said: "It is a command from the commands of God."

Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Then there passed over it a visitation from your Lord while they were asleep﴾ he said: "A command from the commands of God came over it while they were asleep."

The people of interpretation differed about what is meant by al-sarim. Some of them said: it refers to the pitch-black night. Others said: the meaning is: their garden became burned and black, like the dark, pitch-black night.

Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn Askar told me, saying: Abd al-Razzaq told us, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: a shaykh of ours informed us, from a shaykh from Kalb called Sulayman, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿so it became like the black night﴾ he said: "Al-sarim: the night."

He said: Abu Amr ibn al-Ala, may God have mercy on him, said in that:

**On the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿So they called out to one another in the morning, "Go early to your tilth, if you are going to harvest." So they set off, murmuring to one another, "No needy person shall enter it today upon you." And they went early, determined, capable.﴾**

Say, exalted is His remembrance: those people, who were the companions of the garden, called out to one another. "Morning" means: after they had reached the morning. ﴿"Go early to your tilth"﴾, that is, the crop, ﴿"if you are going to harvest"﴾, meaning: if you intend to reap your crop. ﴿So they set off, murmuring to one another﴾, meaning: they went to their tilth, whispering among themselves ﴿"No needy person shall enter it today upon you"﴾, meaning: as they whispered, each said to the other, "Let no needy person enter your garden today against you."

As reported: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿So they called out to one another in the morning, "Go early to your tilth, if you are going to harvest." So they set off, murmuring to one another﴾, he said: "They spoke secretly." ﴿"No needy person shall enter it today upon you."﴾

As reported: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: "When their father died, they went early to it and said: ﴿'No needy person shall enter it today upon you.'﴾"

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of al-hard (intent, determination) in this place. Some of them said: its meaning is: "upon power in themselves and diligence."

Those who said this:

As reported: 'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And they went early, determined, capable﴾, he said: "possessors of power."

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj informed us, from one who narrated to him, from Mujahid, regarding the words of God: ﴿determined, capable﴾, he said: "with diligence, capable in themselves."

Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, regarding His words: ﴿And they went early, determined, capable﴾, he said: "with effort," or he said "with diligence."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And they went early, determined, capable﴾: the people went early, having determined to reach their garden, capable of it in themselves.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿And they went early, determined, capable﴾, he said: "with diligence regarding their affair."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿determined, capable﴾: "with diligence, capable in themselves."

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: they went early upon their affair, which they had agreed upon among themselves, concealed, and kept secret within themselves.

Those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibrahim ibn al-Muhajir, from Mujahid: ﴿And they went early, determined, capable﴾, he said: "There was a tilth belonging to their father, and they were brothers, and they said: 'We will not feed a needy person from it until we know what it yields.' ﴿And they went early, determined, capable﴾: upon a matter they had established among themselves."

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Waqqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿upon determination﴾, he said: "upon a settled matter."

Hannad narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah: ﴿And they went early, determined, capable﴾, he said: "upon a settled matter."

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: they went early in want and need.

Those who said this:

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, who said: al-Hasan said, regarding His words: ﴿And they went early, determined, capable﴾, he said: "in want."

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: in anger.

Those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan: ﴿And they went early, determined, capable﴾, he said: "in anger." It appears that Sufyan, in this interpretation, went to something like the verse of al-Ashhab ibn Rumaylah:

*Lions of Shara met lions of Khufayyah; they gave one another to drink, upon harad, the blood of the lions.* [[This verse is among the witnesses of Abu 'Ubaydah in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 179) at His words, the Exalted: "And they went early, determined." He said: its metaphor is "upon prevention," from "haridat al-naqah" when a she-camel had no milk. And "upon harad" also means "upon intent." The first one said: "A torrent came by God's command, ... it intends the intent of the garden that is bare." And another said: "upon harad" means "upon anger." Al-Ashhab ibn Rumaylah, who used to satirize al-Farazdaq, said: "Lions of Shara..." the verse. Al-Shara and Khufayyah are two well-known thickets of lions. Al-Asawid is the plural of asad, which is a name for a snake, and that is why it is pluralized as names are pluralized on the pattern fa'il, like arani b; had it been an adjective, it would have been pluralized as sud. I say: the wording of the verse in (Lisan: harad) is: "Lions of Shara met lions of Khufayyah, they gave one another to drink poison, all of them harid." Then after the verse, Abu al-'Abbas said: Abu Zayd, al-Asma'i, and Abu 'Ubaydah said: "What we have heard from the eloquent Arabs is: harad yahrad harada like ghadiba yaghdabu ghadaban," with the r vowelled. Abu al-'Abbas (Tha'lab) said: I asked Ibn al-A'rabi about it and he said: it is sound, except that al-Mufaddal reported that among the Arabs are those who say harad harada (like ghadab ghadaban) and harada (with the r sukun), and the sukun is more common. The other is eloquent.]] meaning: upon anger. Some of the people of knowledge of the Arabic language from Basra interpreted it as: "upon prevention."

He directs it to their saying: "haridat al-sanah" when there was no rain in it, and "haridat al-naqah" when she had no milk, as the poet said:

*When she stops giving milk or the udder dries, the hoof of the other one (?) crushes its...* [[In Lisan (harad): haridat al-ibil harad: their milk ceased or diminished. In Lisan (bak'): bak'at al-naqah wa al-shah bukaa' and bakuat, she is bak'i and bakiah: her milk decreased, and it was said: it ceased. Al-Fatt: crushing. Fatta al-shay' yafutuhu fatan: crushed it; and it was said: fattahu: broke it. The author of Lisan cited the verse under harad together with another verse before it, and said: al-harid: the she-camel of little milk, and al-harud of she-camels: of little yield. Harida al-sanah: its water and rain diminished, and it was borrowed for vessels when their drink was exhausted. He said: "And we have a bowl full, a jar followed by its ..."]]

This is a view of which we know no one among the earlier scholars who said it, though it has a basis; since that is so, and since it is not permissible in our view to exceed what the proof has agreed upon, what is sound among the sayings on this matter is only one of the sayings we have mentioned from the people of knowledge. Since that is so, and since the known meaning of harad in the speech of the Arabs is intent, as in their saying: "Fulan harada fulan's harad" when he aimed at his aim; and from it is the saying of the rajaz poet:

*A torrent came by God's command; it intends the intent of the garden that is bare.* [[These are two verses of rajaz, not attributed to a known speaker. Like al-Farra's transmission in Ma'ani al-Qur'an, and the first verse in Lisan (harad) as in the author's version here: "Wa jaa sayl." In Majaz al-Qur'an: "qad jaa." In al-Kamil of al-Mubarrad 1:50, Mustafa al-Babi al-Halabi edition: "qad jaa fi sabil jaa." Al-Mubarrad said in al-Kamil: As for the words of God, Mighty and Majestic, "And they went early, determined, capable," there are two views: one of them is what we mentioned of the meaning of intent; the poet said: "qad jaa sayl jaa..." the two verses. And they said: "upon harad": upon prevention, from their saying "haridat al-sanah" when it withheld its rain, and "haridat al-naqah" when she withheld her milk. End. Al-Farra said in Ma'ani al-Qur'an: "upon harad": upon diligence and capability in themselves. And harad also means intent, as a man says: "qad aqbaltu qablaka, wa qasadtu qasdaka, wa haradtu hardaka." And one of them recited to me: "Wa jaa sayl..." the two verses. He means: its intent. End.]]

It means: intending its intent. It is correct that the view most fitting the interpretation of the verse is the saying of the one who said: the meaning of His words, "And they went early, determined, capable," is: they went early upon a matter they had intended and resolved upon, and kept secret among themselves, capable of it within themselves.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Waqqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿upon determination﴾, he said: "upon a settled matter."

Hannad narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah: ﴿And they went early, determined, capable﴾, he said: "upon a settled matter."

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: they went early in want and need.

Those who said this:

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, who said: al-Hasan said, regarding His words: ﴿And they went early, determined, capable﴾, he said: "in want."

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: in anger.

Those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan: ﴿And they went early, determined, capable﴾, he said: "in anger." It appears that Sufyan, in this interpretation, went to something like the verse of al-Ashhab ibn Rumaylah:

*Lions of Shara met lions of Khufayyah; they gave one another to drink, upon harad, the blood of the lions.* [[This verse is among the witnesses of Abu 'Ubaydah in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 179) at His words, the Exalted: "And they went early, determined." He said: its metaphor is "upon prevention," from "haridat al-naqah" when a she-camel had no milk. And "upon harad" also means "upon intent." The first one said: "A torrent came by God's command, ... it intends the intent of the garden that is bare." And another said: "upon harad" means "upon anger." Al-Ashhab ibn Rumaylah, who used to satirize al-Farazdaq, said: "Lions of Shara..." the verse. Al-Shara and Khufayyah are two well-known thickets of lions. Al-Asawid is the plural of asad, which is a name for a snake, and that is why it is pluralized as names are pluralized on the pattern fa'il, like arani b; had it been an adjective, it would have been pluralized as sud. I say: the wording of the verse in (Lisan: harad) is: "Lions of Shara met lions of Khufayyah, they gave one another to drink poison, all of them harid." Then after the verse, Abu al-'Abbas said: Abu Zayd, al-Asma'i, and Abu 'Ubaydah said: "What we have heard from the eloquent Arabs is: harad yahrad harada like ghadiba yaghdabu ghadaban," with the r vowelled. Abu al-'Abbas (Tha'lab) said: I asked Ibn al-A'rabi about it and he said: it is sound, except that al-Mufaddal reported that among the Arabs are those who say harad harada (like ghadab ghadaban) and harada (with the r sukun), and the sukun is more common. The other is eloquent.]] meaning: upon anger. Some of the people of knowledge of the Arabic language from Basra interpreted it as: "upon prevention."

He directs it to their saying: "haridat al-sanah" when there was no rain in it, and "haridat al-naqah" when she had no milk, as the poet said:

*When she stops giving milk or the udder dries, the hoof of the other one (?) crushes its...* [[In Lisan (harad): haridat al-ibil harad: their milk ceased or diminished. In Lisan (bak'): bak'at al-naqah wa al-shah bukaa' and bakuat, she is bak'i and bakiah: her milk decreased, and it was said: it ceased. Al-Fatt: crushing. Fatta al-shay' yafutuhu fatan: crushed it; and it was said: fattahu: broke it. The author of Lisan cited the verse under harad together with another verse before it, and said: al-harid: the she-camel of little milk, and al-harud of she-camels: of little yield. Harida al-sanah: its water and rain diminished, and it was borrowed for vessels when their drink was exhausted. He said: "And we have a bowl full, a jar followed by its ..."]]

This is a view of which we know no one among the earlier scholars who said it, though it has a basis; since that is so, and since it is not permissible in our view to exceed what the proof has agreed upon, what is sound among the sayings on this matter is only one of the sayings we have mentioned from the people of knowledge. Since that is so, and since the known meaning of harad in the speech of the Arabs is intent, as in their saying: "Fulan harada fulan's harad" when he aimed at his aim; and from it is the saying of the rajaz poet:

*A torrent came by God's command; it intends the intent of the garden that is bare.* [[These are two verses of rajaz, not attributed to a known speaker. Like al-Farra's transmission in Ma'ani al-Qur'an, and the first verse in Lisan (harad) as in the author's version here: "Wa jaa sayl." In Majaz al-Qur'an: "qad jaa." In al-Kamil of al-Mubarrad 1:50, Mustafa al-Babi al-Halabi edition: "qad jaa fi sabil jaa." Al-Mubarrad said in al-Kamil: As for the words of God, Mighty and Majestic, "And they went early, determined, capable," there are two views: one of them is what we mentioned of the meaning of intent; the poet said: "qad jaa sayl jaa..." the two verses. And they said: "upon harad": upon prevention, from their saying "haridat al-sanah" when it withheld its rain, and "haridat al-naqah" when she withheld her milk. End. Al-Farra said in Ma'ani al-Qur'an: "upon harad": upon diligence and capability in themselves. And harad also means intent, as a man says: "qad aqbaltu qablaka, wa qasadtu qasdaka, wa haradtu hardaka." And one of them recited to me: "Wa jaa sayl..." the two verses. He means: its intent. End.]]

It means: intending its intent. It is correct that the view most fitting the interpretation of the verse is the saying of the one who said: the meaning of His words, "And they went early, determined, capable," is: they went early upon a matter they had intended and resolved upon, and kept secret among themselves, capable of it within themselves.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 68, verses 26–28:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿So when they saw it, they said, "Indeed, we have strayed [from the way].  Rather, we are deprived."  The most just of them said, "Did I not tell you, 'Why do you not glorify [Allah]?'"﴾

His saying, exalted is He, means: When these people reached their garden and saw its harvest burned, they denied it and doubted whether it was their garden or not. Some of them said to their companions, thinking that they had lost the way to their garden and that what they saw was other than it: "Indeed, we, O people, have strayed [from the way to our garden]." But the one who knew that it was their garden, and that they had not erred in the way, said: "Rather, we, O people, are deprived; we have been deprived of the benefit of our garden by the loss of its harvest."

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿So when they saw it, they said, "Indeed, we have strayed"﴾: that is, "We have lost the way. Rather, we are deprived. Rather, we have been punished and so deprived."

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿So when they saw it, they said, "Indeed, we have strayed"﴾.

Qatadah said: They said, "We have missed the way; this is not our garden." Then some of them said, "Rather, we are deprived; we have been deprived of our garden."

* *

As for His saying, ﴿The most just of them said﴾:

That is, the most just of them.

The people of interpretation have said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying, ﴿The most just of them said﴾: "The most just of them." It is also said: "The best of them said." And regarding al-Baqarah, ﴿And thus We have made you a median (wasat) nation﴾, he said: "The wasat is the just."

'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying, ﴿The most just of them said﴾: he means "the most just of them."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: al-Furat ibn Khalid narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibrahim ibn al-Muhajir, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿The most just of them said﴾: "the most just of them."

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, ﴿The most just of them said﴾: "the most just of them."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, regarding ﴿The most just of them said﴾: "the most just of them."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿The most just of them said﴾: that is, "the most just of them in speech, and the one who was quickest to be alarmed among the people, and the best of them in turning back," ﴿Did I not tell you, "Why do you not glorify [Allah]?"﴾.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿The most just of them said﴾: "the most just of them."

I was told from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying, ﴿The most just of them said﴾: "the most just of them."

* *

As for His saying, ﴿Did I not tell you, "Why do you not glorify [Allah]?"﴾:

He says: "Why do you not make the exception (istithna')," when you said, ﴿that they would surely harvest it at dawn﴾, so that you would have said, "If Allah wills."

The people of interpretation have said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibrahim ibn al-Muhajir, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Why do you not glorify [Allah]?﴾: he said: "It has reached me that it is the exception (istithna')."

Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Did I not tell you, "Why do you not glorify [Allah]?"﴾: he said: "He says: 'Why do you not make the exception?' So the glorification (tasbih) among them was the exception."

As for His words: ﴿Or do they have partners? Then let them bring their partners, if they are truthful﴾

His exalted remembrance says: Do these people have partners in what they say and describe of matters that they claim belong to them? Then let them bring their partners in that, if they are truthful in what they claim of partners.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 68, verses 37–41:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Or do you have a book in which you study, that indeed you will have therein whatever you choose? Or do you have oaths binding upon Us until the Day of Resurrection, that indeed you will have whatever you judge? Ask them which of them will stand surety for that. Or do they have partners? Then let them bring their partners, if they are truthful.﴾

His exalted remembrance says to the polytheists among the Quraysh: Do you, O people, by your equating between the Muslims and the criminals in the honour of God, have a book sent down from God, brought to you by one of His messengers, stating that you will have what you choose? Then you study in it what you say.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation, i.e., the exegetes) said what we have said on this matter.

Those who said this:

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words: ﴿Or do you have a book in which you study﴾, he said: In it is what you say you read; you study it. And he recited: ﴿Or have We given them a book so that they are upon clear proof from it?﴾ ... to the end of the verse.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Indeed you will have therein whatever you choose﴾

His majestic praise says: Indeed you will have in that, of the matters you choose for yourselves. This is a command from God, a rebuke and reproach to these people for what they used to say of falsehood and for the false wishes they desired.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Or do you have﴾

In it is ﴿oaths binding upon Us until the Day of Resurrection﴾. He says: Do you have oaths upon Us that extend to you until the Day of Resurrection, that indeed you will have what you judge? That is, that you will have your judgment. But the alif of "inna" was given a kasra because the lam entered the predicate: that is, do you have oaths upon Us that you will have your judgment?

* *

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Ask them which of them will stand surety for that. Or do they have partners? Then let them bring their partners, if they are truthful﴾

His exalted remembrance says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Ask these polytheists, O Muhammad, which of them will stand surety for them that they have binding oaths upon Us until the Day of Resurrection concerning their judgment. ﴿Za'im﴾ means: one who guarantees it. Among the Arabs, the za'im is the guarantor and the spokesman for a people.

As:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿Which of them will stand surety for that﴾, he said: Which of them is a guarantor for that.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿Ask them which of them will stand surety for that﴾, he said: Which of them is a guarantor for that.

* *

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 68, verse 42–43 (part 1 of 2):

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day when the shin will be uncovered, and they will be summoned to prostrate, but they will not be able [to do so]﴾ [42] ﴿Their eyes downcast, humiliation covering them. And they had been summoned to prostration while they were sound﴾ [43].

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿On the Day when the shin will be uncovered﴾. A group of the Companions and the Successors (tabi'un) among the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said: it means "when a severe matter will be made manifest."

"The war has stood up against us on a shin [[This is a line of rajaz (mashtur). The author cited it at His words (on the Day when the shin will be uncovered), meaning: a great matter. Abu Ubaydah said in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 179): (on the Day when the shin will be uncovered) when war and matter become severe, it is said: the matter has been uncovered from its shin.]]"

'The war has stood up against us on a shin'?"

• Muhammad ibn Ubayd al-Muharibi and Ibn Humayd narrated to me, both saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿On the Day when the shin will be uncovered﴾: he said: "the severity and seriousness of the matter."
