• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿On the Day when the shin will be uncovered﴾, he said: "about a dreadful, grave matter."

• Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿On the Day when the shin will be uncovered﴾, he said: "The Day when the severity of the matter will be uncovered."

• al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿On the Day when the shin will be uncovered﴾. • Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, who said: Abu al-Zahra' narrated to us, from Abdullah, who said: "God will manifest Himself to creation on the Day of Resurrection until the Muslims pass by. He says: 'Whom do you worship?' They say: 'We worship God; we do not associate anything with Him.' He rebukes them twice or three times, then says: 'Do you recognize your Lord?' They say: 'Glory be to Him; when He introduces Himself to us, we recognize Him.' At that moment the shin will be uncovered, and no believer will remain but he will fall prostrate before God, while the hypocrites will remain with their backs as a single layer, as if there were spikes in them. They will say: 'Our Lord!' He will say: 'You used to be summoned to prostration while you were sound.'"

• Yahya ibn Talhah al-Yarbu'i narrated to me, saying: Shurayk narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "A herald will call out on the Day of Resurrection: 'Is it not just from your Lord, who created you, then fashioned you, then provided for you, then you turned to other than Him, that He should turn over to each of you what you turned to?' They say: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then for every people their gods which they used to worship will be presented, and they will follow them until they bring them to the Fire. And those of the call will remain, and some of them will say to others: What are you waiting for? The people have gone? They will say: We are waiting for us to be called. Then He will come to them in a form,' he mentioned some of it as God willed, 'and He will uncover what God wills to uncover.' He said: 'They will fall down in prostration except the hypocrites, for the vertebrae of their spines will become one bone like the spikes of cattle. It will be said to them: Raise your heads to your light.'" Then he mentioned a story that was lengthy.

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr narrated to us, saying: al-A'mash narrated to us, from al-Minhal, from Qays ibn Sakan, who said: Abdullah related, while he was with Umar, [the verse] ﴿On the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds﴾, and said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, people will stand before the Lord of the worlds for forty years, their eyes fixed upward to the sky, barefoot and naked, the sweat bridling them, and no human will speak to them for forty years. Then a herald will call: 'O people, is it not just from your Lord, who created you, fashioned you and provided for you, then you worshipped other than Him, that He should turn over to every people what they turned to?' They say: 'Yes.' He said: Then for every people what they used to worship besides God will be presented, meaning their gods, and they will follow them until they throw them into the Fire. The Muslims and the hypocrites will remain, and it will be said: 'Will you not go? The people have gone.' They say: 'Until our Lord comes to us.' It will be said: 'Would you recognize Him?' They say: 'If He introduces Himself to us, we will recognize Him.' He said: Then He will manifest Himself, and whoever used to worship Him will fall prostrate. He said: The hypocrites will remain unable [to prostrate], as if their backs were spikes. He said: They will be taken away and driven to the Fire, and they will be thrown into it. And these will enter Paradise, and they will be received in Paradise with what they are received with of reward, wives and the wide-eyed houris; for each man of them in Paradise there will be such-and-such, between each garden such-and-such, between its nearest and farthest part a thousand years, and he sees its farthest part as he sees its nearest. He said: A man of good appearance will meet him, and when he looks at him approaching he will think he is his Lord; so he will say to him: 'Do not do that; I am only your servant and your steward over a thousand villages.'" He said: Umar said: "O Ka'b, do you not hear what Abdullah narrates?"

• Ibn Jabalah narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Abu Awanah narrated to us, saying: Sulayman al-A'mash narrated to us, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Abu Ubaydah and Qays ibn Sakan, who both said: Abdullah said while narrating to Umar, and Umar kept saying: "Woe to you, O Ka'b, do you not hear what Abdullah is saying?" "When people are dragged upon their feet for forty years, their eyes fixed upward to the sky, no human speaking to them, and the sun over their heads until the sweat bridles them, every pious and wicked one among them, then a herald will call from the sky: 'O people, is it not just from your Lord, who created you, provided for you and fashioned you, then you turned to other than Him, that He should turn over to each man among you what he turned to?' They say: 'Yes.' Then a herald will call from the sky: 'O people, let every nation go to what it used to worship.' He said: The mirage will be spread out for them. He said: What they used to worship will be presented to them. He said: They will set off until they enter the Fire. It will be said to the Muslims: 'What holds you back?' They say: 'This is our place until our Lord comes to us.' It will be said to them: 'Would you recognize Him if you saw Him?' They say: 'If He introduces Himself to us, we will recognize Him.'"

He said: Abu Salih narrated to me, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ: "... until one of them turns and the shin is uncovered, and they fall down in prostration. He said: The backs of the hypocrites will be fused until they become one bone, like the spikes of cattle. He said: It will be said to them: 'Raise your heads to your light according to your deeds.' He said: A group of them will raise their heads to light like mountains, and they will pass over the Sirat like the blink of an eye. Then another group will raise their heads to light like palaces, and they will pass over the Sirat like the passing of the wind. Then others will have before them light like houses, and they will pass like the passing of horses. Then others will be raised to a light less than that, and they will be pulled along forcefully. And others below that will walk, until the last of the people remains, a man on the tip of his toe, like a lamp; he will fall once and stand up another time, and the Fire will touch him and scorch him until he emerges, and he will say: 'No one has been given what I have been given,' and he does not know how he was saved, except that 'I found its touch, and I found its heat.'" And he mentioned a lengthy hadith, of which I have abridged this part.

• Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to me, saying: Ja'far ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn Aslam narrated to us, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, a herald will call: 'Let every nation follow what it used to worship.' Not one who used to worship an idol, a statue, or an image will remain, but they will all go until they fall into the Fire. Those who worshipped God alone will remain, both the righteous and the sinful, along with the remnants of the People of the Book. Then Hell will be displayed as if it were a mirage, its parts crushing one another. Then the Jews will be called, and it will be said to them: 'What did you used to worship?' They say: 'Uzayr, son of God.' He says: 'You have lied; God has not taken a consort or a son. So what do you want?' They say: 'O our Lord, we are thirsty, give us drink.' He says: 'Will you not come to the water?' So they go until they fall into the Fire. Then the Christians will be called, and it will be said: 'What did you used to worship?' They say: 'The Messiah, son of God.' He says: 'You have lied; God has not taken a consort or a son. So what do you want?' They say: 'O our Lord, we are thirsty, give us drink.' He says: 'Will you not come to the water?' So they go and fall into the Fire. Then whoever worshipped God remains, both righteous and sinful." He said: "Then God will manifest Himself to us in a form other than the form in which we saw Him the first time, and He will say: 'O people, every nation has gone after what it used to worship, and you remain. None will speak to Him that day except the prophets.' They will say: 'We parted from the people in the world, and we were more in need of their company there. Every nation has gone after what it used to worship, and we are waiting for our Lord whom we used to worship.' He will say: 'I am your Lord.' They will say: 'We seek refuge in God from You.' He will say: 'Is there a sign between you and God by which you know Him?' They say: 'Yes.' Then the shin will be uncovered, and they will all fall prostrate, and no one who prostrated in the world for show, reputation or hypocrisy will remain, but his back will become a single layer, and whenever he wants to prostrate he will fall on his back." He said: "Then He will return, and raise our righteous and our wicked, and He will have returned to us in the form in which we saw Him the first time, and He will say: 'I am your Lord.' They will say: 'Yes, You are our Lord,' three times."

They will say: 'By God, we have no god but God, and we did not worship any god other than Him'; and He is the one who made them firm. Then He will say to them a second time the same: 'Join your gods and what you used to worship.' They will say the same. • Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Asim ibn Kulayb, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "about the severity of the matter."

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿On the Day when the shin will be uncovered﴾, he said: "about a dreadful, grave matter."

• Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿On the Day when the shin will be uncovered﴾, he said: "The Day when the severity of the matter will be uncovered."

• al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿On the Day when the shin will be uncovered﴾. And Ibn Abbas used to say: "The people of the Jahiliyyah used to say: 'The war has rolled up its shin,' meaning the approach of the Hereafter and the passing of this world."

• Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, who said: Abu al-Zahra' narrated to us, from Abdullah, who said: "God will manifest Himself to creation on the Day of Resurrection until the Muslims pass by. He says: 'Whom do you worship?' They say: 'We worship God; we do not associate anything with Him.' He rebukes them twice or three times, then says: 'Do you recognize your Lord?' They say: 'Glory be to Him; when He introduces Himself to us, we recognize Him.' At that moment the shin will be uncovered, and no believer will remain but he will fall prostrate before God, while the hypocrites will remain with their backs as a single layer, as if there were spikes in them. They will say: 'Our Lord!' He will say: 'You used to be summoned to prostration while you were sound.'"

• Yahya ibn Talhah al-Yarbu'i narrated to me, saying: Shurayk narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "A herald will call out on the Day of Resurrection: 'Is it not just from your Lord, who created you, then fashioned you, then provided for you, then you turned to other than Him, that He should turn over to each of you what you turned to?' They say: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then for every people their gods which they used to worship will be presented, and they will follow them until they bring them to the Fire. And those of the call will remain, and some of them will say to others: What are you waiting for? The people have gone? They will say: We are waiting for us to be called. Then He will come to them in a form,' he mentioned some of it as God willed, 'and He will uncover what God wills to uncover.' He said: 'They will fall down in prostration except the hypocrites, for the vertebrae of their spines will become one bone like the spikes of cattle. It will be said to them: Raise your heads to your light.'" Then he mentioned a story that was lengthy.

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr narrated to us, saying: al-A'mash narrated to us, from al-Minhal, from Qays ibn Sakan, who said: Abdullah related, while he was with Umar, [the verse] ﴿On the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds﴾, and said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, people will stand before the Lord of the worlds for forty years, their eyes fixed upward to the sky, barefoot and naked, the sweat bridling them, and no human will speak to them for forty years. Then a herald will call: 'O people, is it not just from your Lord, who created you, fashioned you and provided for you, then you worshipped other than Him, that He should turn over to every people what they turned to?' They say: 'Yes.' He said: Then for every people what they used to worship besides God will be presented, meaning their gods, and they will follow them until they throw them into the Fire. The Muslims and the hypocrites will remain, and it will be said: 'Will you not go? The people have gone.' They say: 'Until our Lord comes to us.' It will be said: 'Would you recognize Him?' They say: 'If He introduces Himself to us, we will recognize Him.' He said: Then He will manifest Himself, and whoever used to worship Him will fall prostrate. He said: The hypocrites will remain unable [to prostrate], as if their backs were spikes. He said: They will be taken away and driven to the Fire, and they will be thrown into it. And these will enter Paradise, and they will be received in Paradise with what they are received with of reward, wives and the wide-eyed houris; for each man of them in Paradise there will be such-and-such, between each garden such-and-such, between its nearest and farthest part a thousand years, and he sees its farthest part as he sees its nearest. He said: A man of good appearance will meet him, and when he looks at him approaching he will think he is his Lord; so he will say to him: 'Do not do that; I am only your servant and your steward over a thousand villages.'" He said: Umar said: "O Ka'b, do you not hear what Abdullah narrates?"

• Ibn Jabalah narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Abu Awanah narrated to us, saying: Sulayman al-A'mash narrated to us, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Abu Ubaydah and Qays ibn Sakan, who both said: Abdullah said while narrating to Umar, and Umar kept saying: "Woe to you, O Ka'b, do you not hear what Abdullah is saying?" "When people are dragged upon their feet for forty years, their eyes fixed upward to the sky, no human speaking to them, and the sun over their heads until the sweat bridles them, every pious and wicked one among them, then a herald will call from the sky: 'O people, is it not just from your Lord, who created you, provided for you and fashioned you, then you turned to other than Him, that He should turn over to each man among you what he turned to?' They say: 'Yes.' Then a herald will call from the sky: 'O people, let every nation go to what it used to worship.' He said: The mirage will be spread out for them. He said: What they used to worship will be presented to them. He said: They will set off until they enter the Fire. It will be said to the Muslims: 'What holds you back?' They say: 'This is our place until our Lord comes to us.' It will be said to them: 'Would you recognize Him if you saw Him?' They say: 'If He introduces Himself to us, we will recognize Him.'"

He said: Abu Salih narrated to me, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ: "... until one of them turns and the shin is uncovered, and they fall down in prostration. He said: The backs of the hypocrites will be fused until they become one bone, like the spikes of cattle. He said: It will be said to them: 'Raise your heads to your light according to your deeds.' He said: A group of them will raise their heads to light like mountains, and they will pass over the Sirat like the blink of an eye. Then another group will raise their heads to light like palaces, and they will pass over the Sirat like the passing of the wind. Then others will have before them light like houses, and they will pass like the passing of horses. Then others will be raised to a light less than that, and they will be pulled along forcefully. And others below that will walk, until the last of the people remains, a man on the tip of his toe, like a lamp; he will fall once and stand up another time, and the Fire will touch him and scorch him until he emerges, and he will say: 'No one has been given what I have been given,' and he does not know how he was saved, except that 'I found its touch, and I found its heat.'" And he mentioned a lengthy hadith, of which I have abridged this part.

• Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to me, saying: Ja'far ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn Aslam narrated to us, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, a herald will call: 'Let every nation follow what it used to worship.' Not one who used to worship an idol, a statue, or an image will remain, but they will all go until they fall into the Fire. Those who worshipped God alone will remain, both the righteous and the sinful, along with the remnants of the People of the Book. Then Hell will be displayed as if it were a mirage, its parts crushing one another. Then the Jews will be called, and it will be said to them: 'What did you used to worship?' They say: 'Uzayr, son of God.' He says: 'You have lied; God has not taken a consort or a son. So what do you want?' They say: 'O our Lord, we are thirsty, give us drink.' He says: 'Will you not come to the water?' So they go until they fall into the Fire. Then the Christians will be called, and it will be said: 'What did you used to worship?' They say: 'The Messiah, son of God.' He says: 'You have lied; God has not taken a consort or a son. So what do you want?' They say: 'O our Lord, we are thirsty, give us drink.' He says: 'Will you not come to the water?' So they go and fall into the Fire. Then whoever worshipped God remains, both righteous and sinful." He said: "Then God will manifest Himself to us in a form other than the form in which we saw Him the first time, and He will say: 'O people, every nation has gone after what it used to worship, and you remain. None will speak to Him that day except the prophets.' They will say: 'We parted from the people in the world, and we were more in need of their company there. Every nation has gone after what it used to worship, and we are waiting for our Lord whom we used to worship.' He will say: 'I am your Lord.' They will say: 'We seek refuge in God from You.' He will say: 'Is there a sign between you and God by which you know Him?' They say: 'Yes.' Then the shin will be uncovered, and they will all fall prostrate, and no one who prostrated in the world for show, reputation or hypocrisy will remain, but his back will become a single layer, and whenever he wants to prostrate he will fall on his back." He said: "Then He will return, and raise our righteous and our wicked, and He will have returned to us in the form in which we saw Him the first time, and He will say: 'I am your Lord.' They will say: 'Yes, You are our Lord,' three times."

• Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Hakam narrated to me, saying: my father and Sa'id ibn al-Layth narrated to me, from al-Layth, who said: Khalid ibn Yazid narrated to us, from Abu Hilal, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "His herald will call, saying: 'Let every people join what they used to worship.' The people of the cross will go with their cross, the people of idols with their idols, and the people of every god with their gods, until there remains only the one who used to worship God, both righteous and sinful, and the remnants of the People of the Book. Then Hell will be brought, appearing as a mirage..." Then he mentioned something similar, except that he said: "We are waiting for our Lord," and he said: "If He says it, then the Mighty One will come to them," then he related to us a hadith similar to the hadith of al-Masruqi.

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Rafi al-Madani, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from a man of the Ansar, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "God will take retribution for the oppressed from the oppressor, until no debt remains owed by anyone to anyone. God will appoint an angel in the likeness of Uzayr, and the Jews will follow him; and God will appoint an angel in the likeness of Jesus, and the Christians will follow him. Then a herald will call, audible to all creation: 'Let every people join their gods and what they used to worship besides God.' No one who used to worship anything besides God will remain but his god will be presented to him before him, and then they will be led to the Fire, until only the believers remain, among whom are the hypocrites. God, exalted is His praise, will say: 'O people, the people have gone, the people have gone; join your gods and what you used to worship.' They will say: 'By God, we have no god but God, and we did not worship any god other than Him'; and He is the one who made them firm. Then He will say to them a second time the same: 'Join your gods and what you used to worship.' They will say the same. It will be said: 'Is there between you and your Lord a sign by which you know Him?' They say: 'Yes.' Then He will manifest to them of His greatness what they will recognize as their Lord, and they will fall down to Him in prostration on their faces, and every hypocrite will fall on his back, and God will make their spines like the spikes of cattle."

• Abu Zayd Umar ibn Shabbah narrated to me, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'id Rawh ibn Junah narrated to us, from a client of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Abu Burdah ibn Abi Musa, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said regarding ﴿On the Day when the shin will be uncovered﴾: "It is about a great light, before which they will fall in prostration."

• Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Buzuri narrated to me, saying: Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' regarding God's words: ﴿On the Day when the shin will be uncovered﴾, he said: "He will uncover the covering." He said: "And they will be summoned to prostration while they are sound."

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Usamah ibn Zayd, from Ikrimah, regarding His words ﴿On the Day when the shin will be uncovered﴾, he said: "It is a day of distress and severity." It is mentioned from Ibn Abbas that he used to read it: ﴿On the Day when the shin will be uncovered﴾, meaning: the Day when the Resurrection uncovers a severe severity. The Arabs say: "This matter has been uncovered from its shin" when it reaches a severe state; and from it is the saying of the poet:
"They uncovered for them its shin, and there appeared from evil the clear [severe] part."

* *

And His words: ﴿And they will be summoned to prostration, but they will not be able [to do so]﴾.

He says: The uncovering of the shin will summon them to prostrate to God, but they will not be able to do so.

* *

And His words: ﴿Their eyes downcast, humiliation covering them﴾.

He says: humiliation from God's punishment will overcome them.

﴿And they had been summoned to prostration while they were sound﴾ — He says: they used to be summoned to prostrate to Him in the world while they were sound, with no obstacle preventing them from it and nothing standing between them and it. It has been said: prostration in this place means the obligatory prayer.

Mention of those who said this:

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, regarding ﴿And they had been summoned to prostration while they were sound﴾, he said: "To the obligatory prayer."

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Sinan, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding ﴿And they had been summoned to prostration﴾, he said: "He hears the caller to the obligatory prayer and does not respond to him."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 68, verse 42–43 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ Qala: Haddathana Mihran, from Sufyan, from his father, from Ibrahim al-Taymi: ﴿And they had been called to prostration while they were sound﴾. He said: "The obligatory prayer (al-salat al-maktubah)."

And in a manner similar to what we have said regarding His words: ﴿And they are called to prostration, but they are not able﴾ ... the verse. The people of ta'wil (interpretation) said:

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Haddathani Ali, who said: Haddathana Abu Salih, who said: Haddathani Mu'awiyah, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And they had been called to prostration while they were sound﴾. He said: "They are the disbelievers, who used to be called (to prostration) in the world while they were safe, and secure; today He calls them while they are fearful. Then Allah, glorified is He, informed that He has placed a barrier between the people of shirk and obedience to Him, both in this world and in the Hereafter. As for in this world, He said: ﴿They were not able to hear, nor did they see﴾. And as for in the Hereafter, He said: ﴿Their eyes will be humbled; they will not be able [to prostrate]﴾."

⁕ Haddathana Bishr, who said: Haddathana Yazid, who said: Haddathana Sa'id, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And they are called to prostration, but they are not able﴾. That is, by Allah, the Day of Resurrection. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "The believers will be permitted on the Day of Resurrection to prostrate, so the believers will prostrate, while between every two believers there is a hypocrite. The back of the hypocrite will stiffen against prostration, and Allah will make the prostration of the believers a rebuke to them, a humiliation, a disgrace, a regret and a sorrow."

* *

And His words: ﴿And they had been called to prostration﴾
That is, in the world, ﴿while they were sound﴾, that is, in the world.

⁕ Haddathana Ibn Abd al-A'la, who said: Haddathana Ibn Thawr, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: It reached me that the believers will be permitted on the Day of Resurrection to prostrate, with a hypocrite between every two believers. The believers will prostrate, and the hypocrite will not be able to prostrate; and I think he said: their backs will stiffen, and the prostration of the believers will be a rebuke to them. He said: ﴿And they had been called to prostration while they were sound﴾.

**The interpretation of His words, exalted is He:** ﴿So leave Me with those who deny this discourse. We will draw them on step by step from where they do not know. And I will give them respite; indeed, My plan is firm.﴾ (44–45)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "Leave, O Muhammad, the matter of these who deny the Qur'an to Me." This is like the saying of one person to another, who threatens a man: "Leave me with him, and let me be with him," meaning: "[He will be harmed] from behind his harm."

The word "مَن" (man) in His words ﴿and those who deny this discourse﴾ is in the accusative position, because the meaning of the sentence is what I have mentioned. It is like the saying: "لو تُركَت ورأيك ما أفلحت" (Had you been left to your own opinion, you would not have prospered). The Arabs put "ورأيك" (and your opinion) in the accusative, because the meaning of the sentence is: "Had I entrusted you to your own opinion, you would not have prospered."

* *

And His words: ﴿We will draw them on step by step from where they do not know﴾

He, exalted is His praise, says: "We will plot against them from where they do not know." This is by granting them the enjoyment of worldly comforts, until they think that they have been given these for their good with God, so they persist in their rebellion. Then He seizes them suddenly while they are unaware.

* *

And His words: ﴿And I will give them respite; indeed, My plan is firm﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: "And I will extend their terms for a lengthy period of time, a long span of age, despite their disbelief and their defiance against God, so that the proofs of God against them may be complete." ﴿Indeed, My plan is firm﴾ means: "Indeed, My plan against the people of disbelief is strong and severe."

**The interpretation of His words, exalted is He:** ﴿So leave Me with those who deny this discourse. We will draw them on step by step from where they do not know. And I will give them respite; indeed, My plan is firm.﴾ (44–45)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "Leave, O Muhammad, the matter of these who deny the Qur'an to Me." This is like the saying of one person to another, who threatens a man: "Leave me with him, and let me be with him," meaning: "[He will be harmed] from behind his harm."

The word "مَن" (man) in His words ﴿and those who deny this discourse﴾ is in the accusative position, because the meaning of the sentence is what I have mentioned. It is like the saying: "لو تُركَت ورأيك ما أفلحت" (Had you been left to your own opinion, you would not have prospered). The Arabs put "ورأيك" (and your opinion) in the accusative, because the meaning of the sentence is: "Had I entrusted you to your own opinion, you would not have prospered."

* *

And His words: ﴿We will draw them on step by step from where they do not know﴾

He, exalted is His praise, says: "We will plot against them from where they do not know." This is by granting them the enjoyment of worldly comforts, until they think that they have been given these for their good with God, so they persist in their rebellion. Then He seizes them suddenly while they are unaware.

* *

And His words: ﴿And I will give them respite; indeed, My plan is firm﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: "And I will extend their terms for a lengthy period of time, a long span of age, despite their disbelief and their defiance against God, so that the proofs of God against them may be complete." ﴿Indeed, My plan is firm﴾ means: "Indeed, My plan against the people of disbelief is strong and severe."

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 68, verses 46–49:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Or do you ask them for a reward, so that they are burdened with debt?﴾ [46] ﴿Or do they have the unseen, so that they can write it down?﴾ [47]

He, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Do you ask these polytheists, O Muhammad, for a reward or recompense for the counsel I have brought them and the truth to which I have called them? ﴿So they are burdened with debt﴾ means: they are weighed down by the debt of that reward. The effort of paying it has burdened them, so they shun accepting your counsel and avoid entering the religion to which you have called them, because of the great weight of the debt that you ask of them in return.

* *

And His words: ﴿Or do they have the unseen, so that they can write it down?﴾

That is, do they have the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz) in which is the report of what is to occur, so that they may copy from it what is in it and argue with you by it, claiming that they, in their disbelief in their Lord, have a higher rank with God than the people of faith in Him?

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿So be patient for the judgment of your Lord, and do not be like the companion of the fish, when he called out while he was distressed.﴾ [48] ﴿Had not a blessing from his Lord reached him, he would have been cast out onto the open wasteland while he was blameworthy.﴾ [49]

He, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): So be patient, O Muhammad, for the decree and judgment of your Lord concerning you and concerning these polytheists, regarding what you have brought them of this Qur'an and this religion. Proceed with what your Lord has commanded you, and let their denial of you and their harm to you not turn you away from conveying what you were commanded to convey.

* *

And His words: ﴿Do not be like the companion of the fish﴾

That is, the one whom it imprisoned in its belly, who was Jonah son of Matta (ﷺ), lest your Lord punish you for abandoning the conveying of that, as He punished him and imprisoned him in its belly: ﴿when he called out while he was distressed﴾ means: when he called out while he was grieved, burdened by sorrow and holding it in.

As:

⁕ Ali narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿when he called out while he was distressed﴾, he said: "distressed" means grieved.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim related to us, he said: Isa related to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿distressed﴾, he said: grieved.

Qatada used to say, regarding His words: ﴿and do not be like the companion of the fish﴾: Do not be like him in hastiness and anger.

Those who said that:

⁕ Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿So be patient for the judgment of your Lord and do not be like the companion of the fish, when he called out while he was distressed﴾, he said: Do not hasten as he hastened, and do not become angry as he became angry.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, the like of it.

* *

And His words: ﴿Had not a blessing from his Lord reached him﴾

He, may His praise be exalted, says: Had a blessing from his Lord not overtaken the companion of the fish, and had He not shown him mercy through it and accepted his repentance for his rebellion against his Lord, ﴿he would have been cast out onto the open wasteland﴾, and al-'Ara' is the open expanse of land. From this is the verse of Qays ibn Ja'da:

"And I raised a leg, unafraid of its stumbling, and cast my garments in the open land" [[The verse is among the examples cited by Abu Ubayda in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 179) at the words of God, "li-nubidha bil-'ara'" (he would have been cast out onto the open wasteland), where he said: "to be thrown onto the face of the earth." A man of Khuza'a called Qays ibn Ja'da, one of the fleeing warriors, said: "And I raised a leg..." the verse]]

﴿while he was blameworthy﴾. The interpreters differed regarding the meaning of His words: ﴿while he was blameworthy﴾. Some of them said: its meaning is "while he was blameworthy" (mulim, one who has committed a fault deserving reproach).

Those who said that:

⁕ Ali narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih related to me, he said: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿while he was blameworthy﴾, he said: "while he was blameworthy" (mulim).

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: "while he was at fault" (mudhnib).

Those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: al-Mu'tamir related to us, from his father, from Bakr, regarding ﴿while he was blameworthy﴾, he said: he was at fault.

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, he said: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, he said: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿would make you slip﴾, he said: they would penetrate you with their eyes.

- Ibn ʿAbd al-Ala narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Mamar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿would make you slip with their eyes﴾, he said: they would strike you down; and al-Kalbi said: they would fell you.

- Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes﴾, they would penetrate you with their eyes, out of hostility to the Book of Allah and to the Remembrance of Allah.

- It was narrated from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes﴾: they would penetrate you with their eyes, out of enmity and hatred.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His saying: ﴿liyuzliqunaka﴾. The majority of the readers of Medina recited ﴿layazliqunaka﴾ with a fatha on the yaʾ, from zalaqtuhu azlaquhu zalfan. The majority of the readers of Kufa and Basra recited ﴿liyuzliqunaka﴾ with a damma on the yaʾ, from azlaqahu yuzliquhu.

The correct view regarding this, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known recitations and two widespread dialects among the Arabs, close in meaning; the Arabs say of one who shaves the head: "He has azlaqahu and zalaqahu." So whichever of the two a reciter uses, he is correct.

* *

And His saying: ﴿when they hear the Reminder﴾

That is: when they hear the Book of Allah being recited, ﴿and they say, "Indeed, he is mad!"﴾. He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: These polytheists whose description has been given say: "Indeed Muhammad is mad, and this which he has brought to us is the raving with which he raves in his madness." ﴿But it is not except a Reminder to the worlds﴾: Muhammad is nothing but a reminder through which Allah reminds the two worlds, jinn and mankind.

End of the commentary on Surah Nun and al-Qalam.
